sample_unit: LLM responses (20 questions x 2 models x 3 sessions), rated by 24 pediatric dentists

links.outcome: Proportion of real versus fabricated references in LLM-generated MIH answers
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o provided 46.5% real and 53.5% fake references; DeepSeek R1 provided 34.2% real and 65.8% fake references.
links.quote: Reference verification revealed notable fabrication rates in both models: ChatGPT-4o provided 46.5% real and 53.5% fake references, while DeepSeek R1 provided 34.2% real and 65.8% fake references.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of response quality across repeated sessions on the same day
links.effect: Both models showed statistically significant but clinically small session-related variations; ICC 0.72 for ChatGPT-4o and 0.77 for DeepSeek R1.
links.quote: Both models showed statistically significant but clinically small session-related variations, with acceptable reliability indicated by ICC values (0.72 for ChatGPT-4o; 0.77 for DeepSeek R1).

links.outcome: Head-to-head expert-rated quality (GQS) of two competing LLMs on MIH questions
links.effect: DeepSeek R1 scored 4.44 ± 0.54 versus ChatGPT-4o 3.99 ± 0.59 (t(23) = 11.83, p < 0.0001); DeepSeek higher across all categories and sessions.
links.quote: When overall scores were examined, DeepSeek R1 (4.44 ± 0.54) again outperformed ChatGPT-4o (3.99 ± 0.59) (t(23) = 11.83, p < 0.0001).

screen.reason: The study empirically assesses the quality, consistency, and citation accuracy of clinical information generated by two LLMs (ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek R1) in response to simulated clinical questions evaluated by pediatric dentists, without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
